```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

`pg_from_vector()` converts homogeneous point, line, or polygon data supplied
as `sf`, `SpatVector`, or a vector-file path. Geometry type is detected by
default, and the available aggregation rules depend on that type.

## Configuration

```{r config}
config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  nrow = 18,
  ncol = 36,
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Points

Point geometries support counts, presence indicators, sums, means, minima, and
maxima. For coordinate tables, `pg_from_points()` is usually more convenient.

```{r points}
points <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(value = c(2, 3, 5), x = c(10, 10.5, 20), y = c(50, 50.5, 60)),
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  crs = 4326
)

point_totals <- pg_from_vector(
  x = points,
  variable = "point_total",
  value = "value",
  aggregation = "sum",
  config = config
)
```

## Lines

Line geometries support total length in metres, length density, distinct
feature counts, and presence.

```{r lines}
roads <- sf::st_sf(
  road_id = 1:2,
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(8, 48, 14, 52), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)),
    sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(18, 58, 23, 62), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)),
    crs = 4326
  )
)

road_length <- pg_from_vector(
  x = roads,
  variable = "road_length_m",
  aggregation = "length",
  config = config
)

head(road_length)
```

## Polygons

Polygon rules include area, cell coverage, feature count, presence, ordinary
value summaries, area-weighted means, and area-weighted allocation of totals.

```{r polygons}
region <- sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
  c(5, 45, 15, 45, 15, 55, 5, 55, 5, 45),
  ncol = 2,
  byrow = TRUE
)))
regions <- sf::st_sf(value = 100, geometry = sf::st_sfc(region, crs = 4326))

coverage <- pg_from_vector(
  x = regions,
  variable = "region_coverage",
  aggregation = "coverage",
  config = config
)

head(coverage)
```

Use `weighted_mean` when overlap areas should weight a rate or continuous
attribute. Use `weighted_sum` to allocate a source polygon total in proportion
to overlap with each cell.

## Groups, dates, and output

`time` assigns one date or year to every feature, while `time_column` maps a
feature-level date column to configured intervals. `group_columns` retains
separate summaries but limits output to `return = "data"`.

Area and length calculations on longitude/latitude geometries require the s2
engine. The package stops with an informative error rather than silently using
planar degree-based measurements.

See `vignette("pg_from_table", package = "priogridR")` when values are stored
in a separate table indexed by polygon identifiers.
